[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "eagle < OE ǣġel/ēagle, via Latin aquila; of = genitive link; death < OE dēaþ; metal < OF metal, from Late Latin metallum",
    "reading": "The soaring sign is yoked to mortality and hard substance: a lofty emblem bound to decay and matter.",
    "languages": ["en", "oe", "la", "of"],
    "source": "OED; Chambers Dictionary of Etymology",
    "confidence": 0.86
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Eagles / eagles; of / off; Death / dearth; Metal / mettle",
    "reading": "Birds become lack: the lofty turns to scarcity, while metal sounds like mettle, suggesting spirit forged under death.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.74
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "eagle ~ aigle (fr); death ~ mort (fr) but death echoes death/dé-; metal ~ métal (fr) and métal ~ mettle by sound",
    "reading": "In French sound, the phrase leans toward the noble bird, then toward death, then toward tempered courage in metal.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.61
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "EAGLES OF DEATH METAL -> THE FATAL MEGA SEED? (partial anagrammatic drift: death + metal + eagles)",
    "reading": "A fatal seed is hidden in the phrase: flight, ending, and hardening rearrange into a compact emblem of doom.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.42
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "Eagles / E; of / O; Death / D; Metal / M -> E.O.D.M.",
    "reading": "Initials condense the phrase into a sealed mark: a fourfold cipher of elevation, linkage, ending, and substance.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.55
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "E = east/exit; O = zero/opening; D = door/decay; M = mountain/matter",
    "reading": "The letters sketch a descent: opening to void, then door of decay, then matter shaped like a mountain.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.49
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "metal < Latin metallum < Greek metallon, 'mine, quarry'; death < OE dēaþ; eagle as emblem of height and sovereignty",
    "reading": "The phrase joins the high emblem to the mined underworld: sovereignty is fused with extraction and death.",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "grc", "oe"],
    "source": "OED; LSJ; Chambers Dictionary of Etymology",
    "confidence": 0.83
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "of death metal -> off-death metal; eagles -> eels/angles by slippage",
    "reading": "What flies becomes what coils or turns: the phrase suggests a crooked passage from sky to underworld.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.38
  }
]
